headline: Marvell has begun sampling two new chips that carry data between AI processors, servers and switches, including one that doubles the reach of its copper cable chips to more than six metres.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a confirmed product launch with company-reported specifications and no customer orders disclosed.
importance_line: Better links inside AI racks help cloud operators pack in more chips and so affect AI service capacity and cost, mainly for the largest cloud companies, but the performance figures are Marvell's own, the chips are only in sampling, and no customer orders were disclosed.
summary: Marvell, a US designer of data-infrastructure chips, announced in a press release on 13 Oct 2026 two connectivity chips that are now being sampled by customers: the Alaska E, a 3.2-terabit-per-second retimer (a chip that cleans up and re-sends a data signal so it can travel further), and a second-generation Alaska A chip for 1.6-terabit active copper cables that Marvell says doubles their reach to more than six metres. Faster links between chips matter as AI systems grow, but customer sampling is an early step and Marvell has not given order volumes.
notes: Credit goes to Marvell's own announcement, which investing.com (the pool item, blocked 403) carried; the 'no order volumes' point comes from GuruFocus.
